messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and for a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a good wipe‑down, remove dust, and tune it to standard pitch (or the key you prefer). | A well‑maintained instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture the body, neck, fretboard, headstock, and any unique features or blemishes. Use natural light and a neutral background. | Great photos attract buyers and reduce the chance of returns. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local classifieds. Note prices for similar models, ages, and conditions. | Helps you set a realistic asking price and avoid over‑ or under‑pricing. | | **4. Write a Detailed Description** | Include brand, model, year, serial number, condition notes (e.g., “no cracks, minor fret wear”), and any accessories (case, strap, picks). | Transparency builds trust and reduces back‑and‑forth. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform(s)** | • **Reverb** – great for musical instruments.
• **eBay** – broad audience, auction or fixed price.
• **Craigslist/Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local Music Stores** – may buy outright or consign. | Different platforms reach different buyer types; use multiple if you’re not in a hurry. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | Start slightly above your target to allow room for negotiation. Consider adding a “price‑match” clause if you’re selling locally. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a buffer keeps you from underselling. | | **7. Decide on Shipping vs. Local Pickup** | • **Shipping**: Use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and a reputable carrier (UPS, FedEx, USPS). Offer tracking and insurance.
• **Pickup**: Meet in a safe, public place (coffee shop, library, police station). Bring a friend if possible. | Shipping expands your market but adds cost; pickup saves money but limits reach. | | **8. Secure Payment** | • **Cash**: safest for local sales.
• **PayPal / Venmo**: offers buyer protection but watch for fees.
• **Escrow services**: for high‑value items. | Protects both parties and reduces fraud risk. | | **9. Handle Negotiations Professionally** | Keep communication polite, respond promptly, and be prepared to justify your price with photos and market data. | Good rapport can close the deal faster. | | **10. Finalize the Sale** | Once payment is confirmed, hand over the guitar, provide a receipt (if requested), and keep a copy of the transaction details. | Documentation protects you in case of disputes. | ### Quick Tips - **Timing**: Spring and summer are peak times for instrument sales as people prepare for music lessons or festivals. - **Condition Disclosure**: Mention any repairs or upgrades (e.g., new strings, pickups) – buyers appreciate honesty. - **Safety First**: For in‑person meetings, choose a well‑lit, public location and let someone know where you’re going. - **Return Policy**: If you’re comfortable, offer a short return window (e.g., 48 hrs) to build buyer confidence. ### Where to List | Platform | Best For | Notes | |----------|----------|-------| | **Reverb** | Musicians, collectors | Free listing, paid promotion available | | **eBay** | General market | Auction or fixed price, global reach | | **Craigslist** | Local | No fees, but requires local pickup | | **Facebook Marketplace** | Local & friends | Easy sharing, no listing fees | | **Local Music Stores** | Direct sale or consignment | May offer instant cash or a commission | --- #### Example Listing > **Title:** 2010 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition > **Description:** > • Brand: Yamaha > • Model: FG800 > • Year: 2010 > • Condition: No cracks, minor fret wear, recently tuned. > • Accessories: Original case, strap, picks. > • Price: $350 (negotiable). > • Shipping: Available (insured). > • Local pickup: Downtown coffee shop, Saturday 10 am–4 pm. > **Photos:** Attach clear images of the front, back, neck, headstock, and any imperfections. Feel free to tweak the price and details to match your guitar’s specifics. Good luck with the sale!

Also mention local music stores, pawn shops. Provide tips for negotiation, payment methods. Possibly mention using the tune_instrument function? But that's for tuning. Not relevant.
